【Prospective Pilot Cohort · deo270457-sec-0090-p1】Consecutive patients undergoing EMR or U‐EMR for colorectal lesions were prospectively enrolled across three outpatient endoscopy units between November 2025 and March 2026. Eligible lesions measured 10–25 mm and were considered suitable for either technique. Lesions with features suggestive of deep submucosal invasion, recurrent or inflammatory bowel disease‐associated lesions, and procedures requiring planned combined or alternative resection techniques were excluded.

【Prospective Pilot Cohort · deo270457-sec-0090-p4】The study protocol was approved by the coordinating center ethics committee (CE Campania 3) (ID 165/26). sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Environmental Impact of Conventional Versus Underwater Endoscopic Mucosal Resection for Colorectal Lesions: A Procedure-Based Life Cycle Assessment With Pooled Effectiveness Estimates》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Forty-nine procedures were included: 23 EMR and 26 U-EMR. En bloc resection was achieved in 56.5% of EMR and 69.2% of U-EMR, and R0 resection in 52.2% and 69.2%. Mean GWP was significantly lower with U-EMR than EMR (1.92 ± 0.54 vs. 2.42 ± 0.50 kg CO2-eq; p = 0.002), corresponding to a reduction of 0.50 kg CO2-eq per procedure and 50 kg CO2-eq per 100 procedures. U-EMR was associated with lower waste generation (324.0 ± 78.3 vs. 407.3 ± 72.0 g; p < 0.001), water consumption (0.56 ± 0.17 vs. 0.77 ± 0.20 m3; p < 0.001), fossil resource scarcity (0.33 ± 0.10 vs. 0.40 ± 0.09 kg oil-eq; p = 0.007), and terrestrial acidification (0.0052 ± 0.0018 vs. 0.0068 ± 0.0018 kg SO2-eq; p = 0.003). Findings were consistent across scenario and uncertainty analyses. In the meta-analysis-based model, GWP per en bloc resection was lower with U-EMR than EMR (2.59 vs. 3.51 kg CO2-eq), corresponding to a 26.3% relative reduction.

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】U-EMR was associated with lower procedure-related environmental burden than conventional EMR, persisting after normalization for en bloc resection.

【FIGURE 1 · deo270457-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 Procedure‐level environmental impact according to resection technique. Box plots show median and interquartile range; diamonds indicate mean values. p‐Values refer to Mann–Whitney U tests comparing EMR and U‐EMR. EMR, endoscopic mucosal resection; U‐EMR, underwater endoscopic mucosal resection; GWP, global warming potential.

【FIGURE 2 · deo270457-fig-0002】FIGURE 2 Effectiveness‐normalized global warming potential according to resection technique. Global warming potential (GWP) was expressed per en bloc resection using pooled en bloc resection rates from randomized controlled trials as the primary effectiveness input. Underwater endoscopic mucosal resection (U‐EMR) maintained a lower GWP per en bloc resection than conventional EMR, indicating that the environmental benefit persisted after accounting for broadly comparable clinical effectiveness.
